progression.prerequisiteKnowledge: B8, B7, B5b, B2b, B1 and Year 10: tracing a parent's alleles into gametes, with letters as labels only (B8); genes code for polypeptides, many proteins are enzymes, genotype and phenotype (B7); homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis I so each gamete gets one of each pair (B5b); pea flowers and self-pollination (B2b); alleles as versions of a gene (B1); one in four and a half (Year 10 probability). Not assumed: dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, Punnett square, test cross, pedigree symbols, carrier, autosome.
progression.startsWith: Mendel's tall pea plants whose short offspring vanished and came back, with the question of how two tall plants can have a short offspring and how a family tree can show the same kind of thing in people.
progression.stopsAfter: Explaining why one allele can hide another; using dominant, recessive, homozygous and heterozygous; building a 2 x 2 Punnett square and reading 1 : 2 : 1 and 3 : 1; saying a ratio is a chance for each offspring and not a guaranteed count; using a test cross; reading pedigree symbols; identifying autosomal recessive and dominant patterns with numbered individuals; turning a pedigree into genotypes and a per-child probability. No sex linkage, no incomplete dominance, co-dominance or multiple alleles, no dihybrid crosses, no conditional probability.
progression.nextLesson: B10: sex linkage and alleles that are not simply dominant or recessive; then G02 for unfamiliar crosses and pedigrees.

teaching.task: Predict offspring with a Punnett square and decide from a pedigree whether an autosomal trait is dominant or recessive.
teaching.causalExplanation: One working copy of a gene can make enough of a protein, so the tall allele shows with one copy and is dominant, while the short allele barely works and shows only with two copies. In meiosis the two chromosomes of each pair separate, so each gamete gets one allele of each gene and a heterozygous plant makes two kinds of gamete in equal numbers. A Punnett square lays out every equally likely fertilisation, so two heterozygotes give 1 : 2 : 1 genotypes and 3 : 1 phenotypes as a chance for each offspring, not a guaranteed count for every group of four. A test cross works because the short parent can only give the short allele, so one short offspring shows the tall parent carries it. In a pedigree, unaffected parents with an affected child must each carry a hidden recessive allele, and affected parents with an unaffected child must each carry a hidden recessive allele that the dominant allele covers, which shows the condition is dominant. Naming numbered individuals is the evidence.
teaching.conversationalApproach: Opens on Mendel's vanishing and returning short plants, explains why one allele hides another with an enzyme, builds the gamete step and the square one box at a time, shows a ratio as a chance with replayed families, uses a test cross, teaches pedigree symbols, traces a recessive and a dominant family generation by generation, gives the hidden-in-the-parents memory aid, then asks two unseen items with a short pause and brief feedback.
teaching.openingDecision: Mendel crossed tall and short pea plants and every offspring was tall, yet when those tall plants self-pollinated 277 of 1,064 were short. How can two tall plants have a short offspring, and how can a family tree tell us the same kind of thing about people?
teaching.understandingCheck: In an unseen autosomal pedigree, say whether the condition is dominant or recessive using numbered individuals, give two genotypes and find the chance that the next child is unaffected. Then round seed by wrinkled seed gives 52 round and 48 wrinkled: find the round parent's genotype with a square and explain why the counts are not exactly 50 : 50.
teaching.curriculumScope: Model the formation of new combinations of genotypes produced during meiosis, including interpreting examples of autosomal inheritance, and construct and interpret information and data from pedigrees and Punnett squares (Module 5, B5-IQ4-02, ACSBL085). Sex linkage, incomplete dominance, co-dominance, multiple alleles, dihybrid crosses and conditional probability are deferred.

design.visualSystem: Explainer engine: warm paper stage, handwritten Caveat headings, amber doodle layer, painted tall and short pea plants, round and wrinkled seed plates, the B5b plum and teal chromosome plates, and coded allele chips, gamete discs, a Punnett grid, a ratio strip, a family replay, a data-driven pedigree with standard symbols and an autosome strip. Allele chips are cream with an ink outline and a printed letter; the top parent is edged plum and the side parent teal. Amber is emphasis only. No people are drawn.
design.transitionPlan: The painted plants open the lesson and carry the cross board from scene 2 to scene 6, with the grid shrinking to the corner for the chance scene; the board wipes to the pedigree board for scenes 7 to 10; each attempt card clears the board and its feedback shrinks the card to a strip and builds the model answer one point at a time; the next chips slide in; scene crossfade with settle.

scenes.visualReference: The painted tall and short pea plants with four tall offspring copies, a coded field of 1,064 plant icons and a small pedigree sketch
scenes.teachingReason: Poses how two tall plants can have a short offspring, using Mendel counts, and previews the family tree
scenes.narrationCue: every one of their offspring grew tall / vanished / pollinate themselves / 1,064 plants / 277 were short / a family tree
scenes.motionPurpose: Tall copies grow in a row, a ghost short plant fades in with a question mark, the field of icons fills to 1,064 and 277 drop short, then a small pedigree sketches in
scenes.onScreenChange: `m5x-pea-tall-v1.png` and `m5x-pea-short-v1.png` stand side by side on a soil strip, joined by a coded "x" (tag "parents"). On "every one of their offspring grew tall" four small copies of the tall plate grow up in a row below (tag "all tall"). On "seemed to have vanished" a ghost outline of the short plant fades beside them with a "?". On "pollinate themselves" a small coded loop arrow circles one tall offspring's flower. On "1,064 plants" a coded field of small plant icons fills a grid (tally ticker counting to 1,064, computed sum 787 + 277); on "277 were short" 277 of the icons drop to short height and a short-plant plate lifts out of the grid beside the ticker "277 short". On "two tall plants have a short offspring" the two tall parents and one short offspring pull to the centre with a bracket. On "a family tree" a small coded pedigree (three symbols, no people) sketches in at the lower right. The heading writes on: "Predicting offspring".

scenes.visualReference: The B8 grey tag struck through, a coded gene to enzyme to hormone chain, a working and a weak enzyme, and allele chips on the stem outlines
scenes.teachingReason: Explains why one allele can hide another through one working enzyme making enough hormone, before naming dominant and recessive
scenes.narrationCue: genes code for proteins / makes a growth hormone / barely works / one of each / dominant / recessive
scenes.motionPurpose: The old tag is struck and replaced by now, enzyme blobs release hormone dots into a stem that lengthens, and the dominant and recessive chips write on beside their plants
scenes.onScreenChange: the cross board's left side. B8's grey tag "which version shows: next video" slides in and is struck through, replaced by "now". On "genes code for proteins" a small gene card with an arrow to a coded enzyme blob (grey tag "B7"). On "makes a growth hormone" the enzyme blob turns small coded hormone dots out into a stem outline, which lengthens. On "barely works" a second enzyme blob with a slightly misshapen pocket makes one hormone dot (tag "barely works"). On "one of each" a stem outline with one working and one weak enzyme still fills with hormone dots and grows tall; `m5x-pea-tall-v1.png` stands beside it. On "dominant" a chip "T" (capital, large serif) writes "dominant: shows with one copy". On "recessive" a chip "t" writes "recessive: shows only with two copies", and `m5x-pea-short-v1.png` stands beside a "t t" card. A grey tag: "genotype: the alleles; phenotype: what you see (B7)".

scenes.visualReference: Three allele cards under tall and short plates, the B5b plum and teal chromosome plates, gamete discs and four offspring cards
scenes.teachingReason: Names homozygous and heterozygous, shows each gamete gets one allele, and explains why the first cross gave all tall
scenes.narrationCue: homozygous / heterozygous / separate / half carry / Mendel's first cross / every one carries the short allele
scenes.motionPurpose: The three cards line up with their tags, the chromosomes slide apart into two gamete discs, four offspring cards drop in and each hidden short allele is ringed
scenes.onScreenChange: on "homozygous" three allele cards line up under three plates: "TT" (tall, tag "homozygous"), "Tt" (tall, tag "heterozygous" on its cue), "tt" (short, tag "homozygous"). Then the "Tt" card opens into B5b's plum and teal single chromosome plates, a "T" chip on the plum and a "t" chip on the teal (grey tag "B5b"). On "separate" the two chromosomes slide apart into two gamete discs (no stage drawing), each keeping one chip: "T" (plum edge) and "t" (teal edge). On "half carry" each disc gets "1/2" (computed). On "Mendel's first cross" the board shows "TT x tt": the TT parent sends only "T" discs, the tt parent only "t" discs; on "all get one of each" four offspring cards "Tt" drop in under four small tall plates; on "every one carries the short allele" each card's "t" chip gets a small amber ring (tag "hidden, not lost").

scenes.visualReference: The coded Punnett grid for Tt x Tt filling box by box with a ratio strip and the hook ticker returning
scenes.teachingReason: Builds the square as every equally likely fertilisation and reads the genotype and phenotype ratios
scenes.narrationCue: across the top / down the side / Each box / Fill them in / 1 to 2 to 1 / Three of the four boxes / 787 to 277
scenes.motionPurpose: Gamete discs slide along the top and side, one chip flies into each box in turn, the ratio rows compute and the ticker returns beside them
scenes.onScreenChange: `PunnettGrid` draws on the right: "Tt x Tt" above it. On "across the top" the plum-edged discs "T" and "t" slide along the top; on "down the side" the teal-edged discs slide down the side. On "Each box" one box pulses with two thin lines from its row and column disc (tag "one fertilisation, chance 1/4"). On "Fill them in" the boxes fill one per cue, each chip flying in from its disc: "TT", "Tt", "Tt", "tt". On "1 to 2 to 1" `RatioStrip` row 1 writes "genotypes: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt" (computed). On "Three of the four boxes" small tall plates pop into three boxes and a short plate into one; row 2 writes "phenotypes: 3 tall : 1 short" (computed by merging). On "787 to 277" the hook's ticker returns beside the strip: "787 : 277 = 2.84 : 1" (computed) with a tag "close to 3 : 1".

scenes.visualReference: The grid shrunk to the corner, rows of four seeds from a seeded draw, a rolling die and a bar chart of short plants per four seeds
scenes.teachingReason: Shows that a ratio is a chance for each offspring, not a count for every group, and that larger samples settle
scenes.narrationCue: not a promise / whatever happened to the seed before it / about 42 per cent / hundreds of seeds
scenes.motionPurpose: Rows of four seeds draw one at a time with different counts, a die rolls above each seed, the bar chart highlights exactly one at 42 per cent and a ticker settles near 26 per cent
scenes.onScreenChange: the grid shrinks to the corner with a tag "1/4 short, for each seed". `FamilyReplay`: rows of four seed plates (`m5x-pea-yellow-round-v1.png` used as a neutral seed token, with a small plant icon that grows tall or short above each) draw one row at a time, outcomes from a seeded random with p = 1/4: row 1 "0 short", row 2 "2 short", row 3 "1 short", row 4 "1 short", row 5 "0 short". On "whatever happened to the seed before it" a small coded die rolls fresh above each seed in turn (tag "each seed: a new chance"). On "about 42 per cent" a bar chart writes on: number of short plants in a group of four (0 to 4) with the "exactly 1" bar highlighted at 42% (computed: 27/64 = 42.2%; other bars 31.6%, 21.1%, 4.7%, 0.4%, labels on bars "0", "1", "2", "3", "4" only, percentages small). On "hundreds of seeds" a ticker runs the hook's 1,064 plants and the short share settles at 26% beside a dashed "25%" line (computed 277/1,064 = 26.0%).

scenes.visualReference: Two tall plates with unknown genotype cards, a short plate and two small grids for the two possible tall parents
scenes.teachingReason: Shows why a test cross works because the tester can only give the short allele
scenes.narrationCue: homozygous or heterozygous / short plant / test cross / even one offspring is short / probably homozygous / more offspring
scenes.motionPurpose: The short plate slides in, both small grids fill, one short offspring removes the question mark from the heterozygous card, and a counter and certainty bar rise for the all-tall grid
scenes.onScreenChange: two tall plates side by side with cards "TT?" and "Tt?" and a tag "same phenotype". A short plate with "tt" slides in below (tag "can only give t"). The grid splits into two small grids: left "TT x tt" fills with four "Tt" boxes (computed, tag "all tall"), right "Tt x tt" fills "Tt, Tt, tt, tt" (computed, tag "1 tall : 1 short"). On "test cross" the label writes over both. On "even one offspring is short" a single short plant icon appears under the right grid and the "Tt?" card loses its "?" with an amber tick. On "probably homozygous" the left grid's tag reads "all tall: likely TT, not proven"; on "more offspring" a counter of tall offspring under it rises 4, 10, 40 while a small certainty bar fills (no number).

scenes.visualReference: A coded pedigree legend and symbols with Roman numerals, individual numbers and an autosome strip
scenes.teachingReason: Teaches the pedigree symbols and numbering so individuals can be named, and says what autosomes are
scenes.narrationCue: pedigrees / Squares are males / shaded symbol / A line joins two parents / Roman numeral / each person a number / autosomes
scenes.motionPurpose: The board wipes to the pedigree board, the legend and a couple with a sibship bar draw in, numerals and numbers write on, and the autosome pairs highlight
scenes.onScreenChange: the board wipes to the pedigree board. A legend writes on at the right, one entry per cue: an open square "male", an open circle "female", a filled square and circle "has the trait". On "A line joins two parents" a square and circle connect with a horizontal couple line; on "a line down" a vertical line drops to a sibship bar with three symbols. On "Roman numeral" "I", "II" write on at the left; on "each person a number" "1, 2" under generation I and "1, 2, 3" under generation II. A grey tag: "carriers are often not marked". On "autosomes" a small coded karyotype strip (22 numbered bar pairs plus an X and Y pair greyed) highlights the numbered pairs (tag "autosomes: not X or Y"). No people, faces or bodies.

scenes.visualReference: Pedigree P1 building generation by generation with travelling allele chips, genotype chips and amber rings
scenes.teachingReason: Shows how unaffected parents can have an affected child because each carries a hidden recessive allele
scenes.narrationCue: two unaffected children / got one recessive allele from him / In generation three / That's the giveaway / carriers / skip a generation
scenes.motionPurpose: Each generation drops in, a recessive chip travels down the lines, amber rings and a bracket mark the giveaway, genotype chips pin and a skip arrow runs across
scenes.onScreenChange: `Pedigree` (data in Numbers, pedigree P1) builds generation by generation. Generation I: I-1 filled square, I-2 open circle. On "two unaffected children" II-2 (open square) and II-3 (open circle) drop in below. On "got one recessive allele from him" a small "a" chip travels down the line from I-1 to each child (genotype chips "Aa" pinned under II-2 and II-3). On "In generation three" II-4 (open square, married in) joins II-3 with a couple line, and III-1 (filled circle) and III-2 (open square) drop in. On "That's the giveaway" II-3, II-4 and III-1 get amber rings and a bracket "unaffected parents, affected child". On "each parent must carry" "Aa" chips pin under II-3 and II-4 and "aa" under III-1. On "carriers" a tag "carrier: has one hidden recessive allele" writes on. On "skip a generation" a soft amber arrow runs from I-1 past generation II to III-1 (tag "skips a generation"). A small assumption tag sits at the lower right throughout scenes 8 to 10: "assume: one gene; the trait always shows when its allele pattern is present; no new mutation".

scenes.visualReference: Pedigree P2 with generation ticks and lines to affected parents, a half-chance grid, an inset trio and a crossed chip
scenes.teachingReason: Teaches the dominant pedigree clues, the decisive affected parents with an unaffected child, and that dominant does not mean common
scenes.narrationCue: every generation / every affected child has an affected parent / a half chance / two affected parents with an unaffected child / dominant doesn't mean common
scenes.motionPurpose: Amber ticks and lines mark the clues, a small grid fills for the half chance, an inset trio shows the decisive pattern and a dominant equals common chip is crossed
scenes.onScreenChange: the board slides to pedigree P2 (data in Numbers). I-1 filled square x I-2 open circle; generation II: II-1 filled circle, II-2 open square, II-3 filled square; II-1 x II-4 (open square, married in): III-1 filled square, III-2 open circle. On "every generation" each generation's filled symbols get a soft amber tick down the left margin, with a grey tag "clues, not proof". On "every affected child has an affected parent" thin amber lines run from II-1 and II-3 up to I-1, and from III-1 up to II-1. On "a half chance" a small grid "Aa x aa" fills beside I-1 and I-2 ("Aa, Aa, aa, aa", computed, tag "1/2 affected, for each child"). On "two affected parents with an unaffected child" a separate inset trio draws (two filled symbols with an open circle child, labelled "inset"), with chips "Aa", "Aa" above and "aa" below; a bracket "affected parents, unaffected child". On "dominant doesn't mean common" a chip "dominant = common" writes on and takes a grey scribble cross, with a tag "Huntington's: dominant and rare".

scenes.visualReference: Two large handwritten rules with trio icons, pedigree P1 returning small with named individuals ringed and a three-part model answer
